entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: 1) The present petition has been filed by the petitioner (wife) seeking transfer of Marriage Petition No.A-149/2024 titled as Rohit Bajpai v. Nimisha Rohit Bajpai @ Nimisha Akhilesh Mishra filed by the respondent (husband) under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 from Family Court, Thane, Maharashtra to Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh.

entities.text: Rohit Bajpai v. Nimisha Rohit Bajpai @ Nimisha Akhilesh Mishra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Court, Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2) As per order dated 25.09.2024, by mutual consent, the parties were relegated to take recourse to mediation before the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.
As per the report dated 10.12.2024 received from the Mediation Centre, mediation between the parties remained unsuccessful.
TRANSFER PETITION (CIVIL) NO. 1745 OF 2024 3)

Learned senior counsel appearing for the respondent has consented for transfer but to Varanasi,
inter alia, stating that three other cases which are pending at Mirzapur may also be transferred to Varanasi where the parental house of the wife is situated, which fact is controverted by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner (wife).
It is further contended that the respondent is a pilot and Varanasi would be convenient for him to attend the proceedings which may not cause any delay.

4) Having considered the submissions of the learned counsels for the parties and in view of the foregoing, in our view also, looking to the educational qualification of the petitioner (wife) and other attending facts and circumstances as placed before us, we deem it appropriate to transfer Marriage Petition No.A-149/2024 titled as Rohit Bajpai v. Nimisha Rohit Bajpai @ Nimisha Akhilesh Mishra filed by the respondent (husband) under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 to Varanasi in place of Mirzapur.

5) We request the District Judge, Varanasi to assign these matters to competent Court, and if possible, to one Court with a note that if it is not inconvenient to the parties, one date may be fixed in all the cases.
